note: No reported movement of Russian forces toward the Baltic states as of 22 October. Long-term construction continues near Finland (a new garrison in Karelia for the 44th Army Corps), which is a structural build-up, not a sign of imminent action.
evidence: OSINT monitoring; satellite investigations by Nordic and Baltic broadcasters

note: Satellite imagery from 23 October shows a fourth cargo ship loading armoured and logistics vehicles at Baltiysk, after three ships on 15–16 October. Destination unknown; these ships have previously carried equipment to Russia's Africa Corps via Libya. A Su-30 crashed on a training flight on 21 October. A large over-the-horizon radar is under construction near Gvardeysk.
evidence: Satellite imagery (GeoInsider, SONARROW); Russian and Ukrainian reporting

note: A five-day CSTO drill with over 1,500 troops in Vitsebsk region, which borders Latvia and Lithuania, began 12 October and has ended. No new drills near the borders reported since. An exiled Belarusian group claims infrastructure is being prepared for a push toward the Suwałki Gap by spring 2027; this is a single, partisan source.
evidence: CSTO and BelTA announcements; opposition claims (unverified)

note: No major Russian or Belarusian exercise near the Baltic borders currently announced. Kaliningrad does not appear on the Russian defence ministry's current exercise lists.

Persistent. Poland's telecom institute linked disruption on most summer days to electronic warfare in the region, traced to Kaliningrad. Baltic authorities reported a sharp rise affecting shipping in September. NATO is now buying its own jamming kits to train against it.
evidence: Government agencies; maritime and aviation monitoring

note: 18 October: a drone, most likely Ukrainian and probably diverted by Russian jamming, exploded in Lithuania and hit a car. Lithuania says it came from Poland; Poland's radars saw no crossing. 13 September: a drone flew from Belarus across Lithuania into Kaliningrad. One independent tracker counts 96 European violations in the last 12 months, against 19 in the 12 before.

28 October: two Belarusians arrested in Germany for plotting arson on infrastructure near Nuremberg, reportedly for Russia. A Ukrainian was arrested in Warsaw in the same case. Romania's intelligence service says a Moscow-run network burned a defence plant in Brașov on 14 September. Germany formally blamed Russia for the 4 August Leipzig airport drone bomb.

5–6 October: armed, masked escorts pushed about 20 migrants at Latvia's border and threatened soldiers; masked people later crossed and stole border cameras. Latvia stopped 11,384 crossing attempts between January and 24 September.
evidence: Latvian armed forces and interior ministry

note: A late-September note to NATO threatened nuclear use if Kaliningrad is isolated; Putin repeated the line on 1 October. Zakharova called possible US troop deployments in the Baltics an escalation on 8 October. Putin says Russia has no plans to attack NATO. No new escalation found this week.
evidence: Official statements; diplomatic note reported by Reuters

note: No mobilization decree. Analysts describe a quiet, year-round call-up instead, aimed at the Ukraine front. Lithuania cited expected Russian mobilization when it sent about 100 troops to the Kaliningrad border from 7 to 16 October.

Unconfirmed: a September report citing anonymous Russian sources says Russia plans 16,000–20,000 extra military beds in civilian hospitals, mainly in the Northwest but also around Moscow and Smolensk. That pattern also fits Ukraine casualties. No field hospitals reported near Baltic borders.
No public reporting of blood supplies moved toward Baltic borders. Absence of reporting is not proof of absence: this sign usually surfaces late, through Western officials.

indicator: Rail transport toward the Baltic direction
note: One report (12 October) that a Belarusian border base was fitted to receive military trains of up to 60 railcars. No reports of equipment trains moving toward Baltic borders.
